title: Content hand-off
description: How the DIGITAL hand-off happens for this order's exchange — the twin of the physical hand-off clause, for value added in the digital medium (a production chain's cut, a design file, a dataset, an access credential; the freelancer's deliverable). Each bonded order with a digital deliverable carries its own content hand-off. Completion evidence is the delivered artifact's keccak256 content hash, filed as a runtime attestation at stage 1 and merkle-bound to the agreement — any counterparty verifies by rehashing what it received. Compose figaro-geolocation ALONGSIDE for territory/jurisdiction geofencing (a licensed territory, the jurisdiction of the work) — geofencing is that clause's concern, never fields here.

fields.name: contentHandoff
fields.description: How the digital exchange happens. encrypted-transfer = the artifact (or its decryption key) travels the per-order ECDH channel, counterparty-private; repository-grant = the counterparty is granted access at a named repository or platform; public-release = openly published, verified by content hash alone. At least one must be set when this clause is included in an agreement.

1.name: contentHash
1.label: Delivered content hash
1.description: keccak256 of the delivered artifact's bytes — the completion evidence. A counterparty verifies by rehashing what it received.

1.name: contentUri
1.label: Content locator
1.description: Optional network locator for the delivered artifact (e.g. ipfs://…) — for public-release and repository-grant modes; omit for counterparty-private transfers.
